title: Prayer for Deliverance
overview: Psalm 140 is a heartfelt plea by David for protection against violent and deceitful enemies. The psalmist vividly describes the malicious intent and harmful speech of his adversaries, asking God to preserve him from their traps and schemes. Throughout the chapter, David expresses his trust in God as his refuge and strength, confident that the Lord will uphold justice for the afflicted and humble the proud. This psalm reflects the broader biblical theme of God as a righteous judge who defends the innocent and punishes the wicked, encouraging believers to rely on divine protection amid spiritual and physical threats.
structure:
**Verses 1-5: The Plea for Protection.** David opens by urgently asking God to deliver him from evil and violent men who plot harm with malicious intent and deceitful speech. He describes their traps and snares, emphasizing the danger they pose.

**Verses 6-7: Affirmation of Faith.** The psalmist declares his personal relationship with God, acknowledging Him as his God and the source of his salvation and protection in times of conflict.

**Verses 8-11: Prayer for Justice Against the Wicked.** David petitions God to frustrate the desires and schemes of the wicked, invoking vivid imagery of divine retribution to prevent their exaltation.

**Verses 12-13: Confidence in God’s Justice and Praise.** The psalm concludes with David’s assurance that God will defend the afflicted and uphold righteousness, prompting the righteous to give thanks and dwell in God’s presence.

keyVerses.text: Deliver me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;
keyVerses.significance: This opening verse sets the tone of the entire psalm as a cry for divine deliverance from hostile enemies. It highlights the believer’s dependence on God’s protection against both moral and physical threats.

keyVerses.text: I said unto the LORD, Thou art my God: hear the voice of my supplications, O LORD.
keyVerses.significance: Here David affirms his personal relationship with God, appealing to God’s faithfulness and inviting Him to hear his earnest prayers. It underscores the intimate trust between the psalmist and the Lord.

keyVerses.text: Grant not, O LORD, the desires of the wicked: further not his wicked device; lest they exalt themselves. Selah.
keyVerses.significance: This verse is a direct plea for God to thwart the plans of the wicked, preventing their pride and success. It reflects the biblical theme that God opposes the proud and supports the humble.

keyVerses.text: I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and the right of the poor.
keyVerses.significance: David expresses confident assurance that God is a just judge who defends the vulnerable. This verse encapsulates the psalm’s message of divine justice and care for the oppressed.

keyVerses.text: Surely the righteous shall give thanks unto thy name: the upright shall dwell in thy presence.
keyVerses.significance: The psalm closes with a note of praise and hope, affirming that those who live righteously will enjoy God’s presence and blessing, reinforcing the ultimate security found in Him.

characters.name: David
characters.description: The psalmist and king who authors this prayer, expressing his distress over violent enemies and his deep trust in God’s protection and justice.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: God is portrayed as the protector, deliverer, and righteous judge who hears prayers, preserves the faithful, and punishes the wicked.

characters.name: The Wicked and Violent Men
characters.description: David’s adversaries who plot evil, use deceitful speech, and set traps to harm him. They symbolize opposition to God’s people and the forces of evil.

themes.description: The psalm emphasizes God’s role as a refuge and shield for the righteous against violent and malicious enemies, a recurring biblical theme affirming God’s care for His people.
David’s earnest supplications demonstrate the believer’s access to God in times of trouble, highlighting prayer as a vital means of seeking divine intervention and comfort.
The psalm reflects confidence that God will judge the wicked and uphold the cause of the oppressed, reinforcing the biblical truth that God is a righteous judge who vindicates His people.
The vivid imagery of snares, poison, and fire illustrates the destructive nature of evil intentions and speech, warning believers to be vigilant against spiritual and physical threats.

historicalContext:
Psalm 140 is traditionally attributed to King David, placing it in the context of ancient Israel during the united monarchy period around the 10th century BC. David faced numerous enemies, both external and internal, including violent men who sought to harm him physically and undermine his reign. The psalm reflects the realities of ancient Near Eastern political instability, where kings often contended with conspiracies and warfare. The cultural context includes the use of poetic imagery common in Hebrew worship and the role of the chief musician in temple worship, indicating this psalm was likely used liturgically.

Geographically, the psalm is set within the land of Israel, a region frequently contested by neighboring peoples. The political situation was marked by tribal conflicts and threats from surrounding nations, making appeals for divine protection essential for survival and leadership. The psalm’s emphasis on God’s justice also reflects Israel’s covenantal understanding of God as their sovereign protector and judge.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God’s sovereignty and justice in this psalm, seeing David’s prayer as an example of trusting God’s providential protection and righteous judgment against evil. The psalm encourages believers to rely wholly on God’s grace rather than human strength.

Dispensational interpreters often view this psalm as prophetic, foreshadowing the spiritual warfare believers face and the ultimate defeat of evil through Christ. The prayer for deliverance is seen as applicable both to David’s historical situation and to the church’s ongoing spiritual battles.

Early church fathers interpreted this psalm allegorically, viewing the violent men as representing the devil and his demons. They saw David’s deliverance as a type of Christ’s victory over sin and Satan, encouraging believers to seek refuge in God’s power.

application: Trust God as your refuge when facing opposition or danger, knowing He hears your prayers.
Pray earnestly and specifically for protection against evil influences and harmful intentions.
Reject pride and deceit in your own life, remembering God opposes the proud and supports the humble.
Rest in the assurance that God will bring justice for the oppressed and punish the wicked in His perfect timing.
Live uprightly to dwell in God’s presence and give thanks for His faithfulness.
Be vigilant against spiritual attacks, using prayer as a weapon to resist the schemes of the enemy.
conclusion: Psalm 140 powerfully captures the believer’s urgent cry for divine protection amid hostile threats, balanced by a confident trust in God’s justice and salvation. It reminds Christians today that God is both a refuge and righteous judge who hears prayers and defends the vulnerable. By meditating on this psalm, believers are encouraged to pray fervently, reject evil, and rest in the assurance that God’s justice will prevail. Ultimately, Psalm 140 calls the faithful to live uprightly and dwell in God’s presence, confident that He sustains and delivers His people through every trial.
